macro.title: What It Means For VWRA, Global Bonds, Gold And Bitcoin

reads.label: World equities
reads.text: carry the adjustment, because 2.66 per cent is the highest real cost of capital this cycle has taken into a drawdown: down 2.97 per cent from the 4 November high, still 1.14 on the week.

reads.label: Global bonds
reads.text: hedged, barely — insurance, not a position, and the week’s one reassuring number.

reads.label: Gold
reads.text: prices the dollar and the haven, not the real yield: up 1.69 per cent as the dollar fell 0.61, yet still lower on the month, because a 2.66 real yield is punishing carry on an asset that pays nothing.

reads.label: Bitcoin
reads.text: prices liquidity alone and fails the haven test outright.

stories.kicker: The World · The Strait and the Mediator
stories.headline: Qatar’s prime minister carried Iran’s Hormuz proposal into the Oval Office
stories.dek: Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani saw President Trump for about forty-five minutes on Monday, closed to press. Doha’s foreign ministry has posted nothing since 7 November; oil fell about five per cent anyway.

stories.kicker: Technology · The Board and the Founder
stories.headline: Nvidia’s board opened an independent investigation into its founder, Jensen Huang
stories.dek: A committee of independent directors will examine whether Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort. The shares closed down 4.27 per cent on Monday while every other big chip name rose.

stories.headline: HEMA rebuilds European swordfighting out of the books its masters wrote
stories.dek: Wiktenauer’s free library holds 23,459 uploaded files; the global ladder lists 21,423 fencers and 418,696 recorded fights. Germany’s federation counts 4,135 people, against more than 23,000 Olympic fencers.

stories.headline: LTA halted ComfortDelGro’s driverless U-turns at Punggol, a day after Grab’s
stories.dek: Two operators, two Punggol near-misses, about two hours apart on 5 November. In both, a human safety operator took the wheel — and at Edgedale Plains in January the authority found the takeover was what caused the crash.

stories.kicker: Buy It Once · Secateurs & Garden Tools
stories.headline: Felco sells every part of the Felco 2, including the washer
stories.dek: The Swiss pruner costs CHF 76.90 and has more than twenty listed spare parts. A Yamagata forge will hand-make you a better-cutting one for ¥9,900 — and sell you nothing to repair it with.

stories.kicker: The Kit · The Aura Price Cut
stories.headline: XREAL cut the Aura’s price and is refunding early buyers
stories.dek: The Android glasses now start at $1,099, down $180 from the price set on 7 October, and begin shipping in mid-November to four countries. Singapore is not one of them.

stories.kicker: The Good Life · The Halo and the Total
stories.headline: Horologer Ming opens orders for the CHF 10,900 Halo tonight
stories.dek: One hundred and fifty pieces, time only, in a titanium case heat-treated until its grain shows. Four days after a Geneva sale that finally published the total this desk had to add up itself.

stories.headline: Godzilla Minus Zero led both Japan and America at once
stories.dek: Takashi Yamazaki’s sequel opened to an estimated US$31.61m from 3,254 American screens and about 690,000 admissions at home — the first Japanese live-action film to lead both markets in the same weekend.

stories.kicker: The Family Desk · Problem Use, Not Hours
stories.headline: A German study separates problem use from screen hours
stories.dek: Across 34,712 German schoolchildren, problematic social media use doubled from 5.3 to 11.1 per cent between 2018 and 2022 — and carries about four times the association with mental-health complaints that heavy online chatting does.

stories.kicker: The Macro Desk · The Breakeven Stops Working
stories.headline: Falling Brent stopped easing financial conditions once real yields rose
stories.dek: The ten-year inflation breakeven in America fell another eight basis points from 3 November to 2.22 per cent, while the ten-year real yield rose four to 2.66. October inflation prints after this edition closes — with no annual rate at all.

stories.headline: Brad Schoenfeld’s team found fixed two-minute rests matched self-chosen ones
stories.dek: Forty trained lifters, eight weeks, lower body only: in Schoenfeld’s trial the differences in muscle growth and strength were trivial, but the fixed group finished each session in 56 minutes against 78.5.

stories.headline: Gardens by the Bay dated Christmas Wonderland and published no prices
stories.dek: The dates went up this week: 27 November to 3 January, 6.30pm to 11pm at Supertree Grove. The ticket line on the same page reads, for the fifth issue running, “Ticket prices will be released soon.”

stories.headline: Japan’s NISA poor starve themselves to fill Tokyo’s tax allowance
stories.dek: 「NISA贫乏」 reached the floor of the Diet in March and the shortlist for Japan’s 2026 word of the year on 5 November. Accounts passed 30,480,850 in June, and purchases ¥85 trillion against a government target of ¥56tn.
